src.q: Cases of QT interval prolongation and arrhythmia have been reported during the post-marketing period.

notes: Batch P (2026-10-17). (1) Fluoxetine: emc 5358 from the clinic monograph is a dispersible-tablet SmPC, not the clinic's capsule; only the 20 mg capsule SmPC (emc-11909) was used. (2) Rowatinex: the brief expected no UK product, but a UK licence exists (PL 00007/0003R) with an SPC and PIL on MHRA products (found through the MHRA products search index; emc has no entry). The SPC text is old (revision 29/06/2004). SPC 4.3 says 'None known' but the PIL says do not take if allergic; both kept, the allergy rule cites the PIL. The PIL title line lists 'Menthone, Menthol' while its section 6, and the SPC, list fenchone and anethol; the SPC composition was used. The SPC gives no child dose; the PIL says under 18 should not take it (age rule cites the PIL). (3) Cystone: no UK product information. Searched emc (trade name 'cystone', 'Himalaya', and ingredients didymocarpus, saxifraga, rubia, shilajit) and the MHRA products index (cystone, Himalaya, shilajit, cordifolia, onosma, vernonia, achyranthes, cyperus, pashanbheda, bergenia, didymocarpus): no matching SPC, PIL or THR. Marked no-uk-product. (4) QT group: amitriptyline and escitalopram added to qt-prolonging. Fluoxetine and mirtazapine were NOT added: SPS says fluoxetine has no effect on QTc at licensed doses, and the mirtazapine SmPC 5.1 says QTc prolongation stayed below the threshold for clinical meaning, although both SmPCs report post-marketing QT cases and advise caution with QT-prolonging drugs (their own rules toward group:qt-prolonging are kept). (5) Escitalopram vs SPS/MHRA: the SmPC says breastfeeding is not recommended; SPS says it can be used with caution. Fluoxetine/amitriptyline/mirtazapine SmPCs ask for a risk-benefit decision; SPS says use with caution. Kept as separate rules. (6) Escitalopram maximum doses for over-65s (10 mg) and hepatic impairment (10 mg) come from the MHRA 2011 DSU; the current SmPC 4.2 says the same through dose steps (5 mg start, up to 10 mg). (7) cyp2c19-inhibitor members omeprazole and fluconazole are sourced from the escitalopram SmPC list; fluoxetine from the sertraline SmPC (emc-1070). (8) Interactions with medicines outside the master list (metoprolol in heart failure, tamoxifen, linezolid, lithium, phenytoin, cimetidine, thioridazine, etc.) are mentioned only in the tables. (9) The emc search page and the fetchtext --links filter returned no links from this location; emc was searched by fetching the search page directly. AUDIT (second check, 2026-10-17, see audit/P-Q.md): Rowatinex licence re-checked in the MHRA products search index: PL 00007/0003R SPC and PIL are listed (documents dated 25 Sep 2026), so the product is on the current MHRA products register; the SPC text itself is still the 2004 revision. Cystone re-checked: no emc result and no MHRA products document. Amitriptyline qt-prolonging membership now also cites SmPC 4.8 (QT prolonged listed as common). New elderly rules: fluoxetine (dose, 40 mg/day guidance) and mirtazapine (caution); both SmPCs say only 'elderly', so 65 years is used as the trigger and the concern says so. Integrator: SPS says sertraline has no QTc effect at licensed doses, yet batch D lists sertraline in qt-prolonging; with the escitalopram contraindication rule this makes escitalopram + sertraline 'contraindicated' through the QT route (review batch D).
